correctness.rationale: The lower bound holds samplewise by the minimum hyperedge count f_H(|S|), then by convex minorization and Jensen at E|S|=nq. For each face of the lower hull, vertex-transitive automorphism averaging of one optimal set at each endpoint gives exactly equal per-vertex inclusion probabilities and preserves the hyperedge count; two-point mixing reaches the lower bound for every q including endpoints. The cycle profile f(s)=max(0,2s-n) follows from 2s=2e(S)+boundary and explicit independent sets or independent complements. The integer slopes 0/1/2 (odd) and 0/2 (even) prove the stated branches, and exact arithmetic verifies 8184 finite deterministic states as a supplementary check. No finite experiment substitutes for the unrestricted proof.

originality.rationale: The primary inspected ecological texts study knockout sequences and model variation, not unrestricted Bernoulli coupling envelopes. Symmetric marginal correlation feasibility is already established and is not claimed anew; this unified result supplies an explicit all-marginal extremum on vertex-transitive ecological incidence hypergraphs and a sharp evaluated even/odd cycle law. The broad 2006 Bernoulli-feasibility paper is an explicitly acknowledged unresolved implicit-coverage risk, but its accessible abstract does not directly state the exact hypergraph/cycle claim.
residual_risks: Full text of Chaganty–Joe (2006) was not accessible; its general Bernoulli correlation feasibility conditions may give a stronger explicit or implicit coverage than can be determined from the abstract.
Older fixed-magnetization antiferromagnetic cycle / Fréchet-class extremal literature not indexed by searched language may contain equivalent phase diagrams.
The q=1/2 symmetric Bernoulli cut-polytope and pairwise Fréchet bounds are known; neither is claimed as new in isolation.
The dependence laws that attain the bound might not be physically realizable in a specified ecological process.

value.rationale: Coextinction risk depends on unknown primary-failure dependence, so the precise best-case envelope at fixed observed individual extinction rates is a natural ecological robustness benchmark. Vertex transitivity reduces the full joint-law problem to a concrete edge-isoperimetric convex profile. The exact cyclic result proves a global parity obstruction to simultaneously realizing individually optimal pairwise Fréchet bounds: a half-plant residual at balanced marginals on every odd cycle, versus zero on even cycles, and gives the full threshold interval for all marginal q. That quantifies a structural boundary beyond textbook independent-loss or pairwise-negative-correlation calculations. Ecological implementability and empirical prevalence are not inferred.
